skill.name: fetching-library-docs
skill.description: Fetches library API documentation through Context7 MCP and filters results into focused examples, API signatures, and notes.
skill.summary: Fetch focused library documentation with Context7 MCP and shell-based filtering.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown examples, code fences, and fixed text filters. Confirmed risks remain: shell-based MCP execution, shell=True stdio process spawning, unpinned npx package execution, network-capable MCP requests, and predictable /tmp PID files.

remediation.issue: The MCP stdio client uses shell=True for a user-provided command string.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with argv-list execution, or restrict stdio commands to a small allowlist.

remediation.issue: The scripts execute @upstash/context7-mcp through unpinned npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version, verify the source, and require explicit approval before first execution.

remediation.issue: JSON parameters are assembled with direct shell string interpolation.
remediation.suggestion: Build MCP parameters with a JSON encoder and validate library, topic, mode, and page values.

remediation.issue: Server helpers trust predictable PID files in /tmp for process control.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private runtime directory, validate numeric PIDs, check process ownership, and avoid broad pkill patterns.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The helper scripts run the Context7 MCP server through npx without a pinned version. A compromised or changed npm package could execute arbitrary local code during normal skill use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts explicitly invoke npx with @upstash/context7-mcp and no version pin. Runtime package execution is a clear supply-chain risk, even if the package is intended.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe PID File Process Control
semantic_findings.description: The server helpers store and trust a predictable PID file under /tmp and then use its contents for kill operations. The stop helper also uses a broad pkill pattern based on the port value.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts show a fixed /tmp PID path and process termination based on that file. The risk is local tampering and unintended process termination, not remote code execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped JSON Parameter Construction
semantic_findings.description: Library and topic arguments are inserted directly into JSON strings before calling the MCP tool. Quotation characters in user-provided values can break or alter the JSON request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds JSON with shell string interpolation rather than a JSON encoder. The impact is limited to MCP parameters, but malformed input can change request structure or fail unexpectedly.

content.value_statement: Library API answers often require large documentation payloads. This skill fetches Context7 documentation and filters it into focused examples, signatures, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Resolves common library names to Context7 library IDs.
Fetches documentation through the Context7 MCP server.
Filters large responses into examples, signatures, and notes.
Supports topic, mode, and page arguments.
Includes helper scripts for raw fetches and extraction.
limitations: Requires Python, Bash, npx, and the Context7 MCP package.
Runs network requests and external commands during use.
Depends on Context7 coverage and library ID quality.
Does not inspect local repositories or private source code.

use_cases.title: Answer Framework API Questions
use_cases.description: Fetch focused examples for React hooks, Next.js routing, Prisma queries, and similar library topics.

use_cases.title: Compare Usage Patterns
use_cases.description: Review examples and signatures across multiple documentation pages before choosing an implementation approach.

use_cases.title: Create Concise Learning Notes
use_cases.description: Collect introductory documentation and important notes for a new package without loading full pages into context.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Basic Examples
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to fetch React useState documentation in code mode and summarize the main usage pattern.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a familiar framework feature.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve A Library First
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Context7 library ID for Prisma, then fetch query documentation with examples and important notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate lookup when the exact library ID is unknown.

prompt_templates.title: Research A Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch Next.js routing documentation in info mode and explain the main routing model in concise bullets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Conceptual research for a framework decision.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Multiple Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch pages one and two for React hooks documentation, compare the examples, and identify advanced patterns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced research that needs broader documentation coverage.

output_examples.input: Fetch React hook documentation for useEffect.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with selected examples, common signatures, and notes about dependency behavior.

output_examples.input: Find Prisma query syntax for filtering records.
output_examples.output: A focused summary of relevant query patterns, important options, and cautions from the documentation.

output_examples.input: Explain Next.js routing using current docs.
output_examples.output: A short conceptual overview with routing terms, selected examples, and follow-up topics to inspect.

best_practices: Use specific topics to reduce irrelevant documentation.
Use known Context7 library IDs when available.
Review security warnings before allowing external commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for private repository analysis.
Do not run helper scripts from untrusted modified copies.
Do not treat fetched examples as reviewed production code.

faq.question: What does this skill fetch?
faq.answer: It fetches public library documentation available through Context7 MCP.

faq.question: Does it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. It needs network access to the Context7 MCP package and documentation service.

faq.question: Can it read my local codebase?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for public library documentation, not local source inspection.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it filter documentation?
faq.answer: Filtering reduces context usage by returning selected examples, signatures, and important notes.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Automatic use needs caution because the skill runs external commands and network requests.
